key_concepts: [url]Creating an Ammo Crate for 3D printing - Full Workflow^^https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BAIqlKUta-U[/url]

content: Start with a cube, and [k]S,Y,1.5[/k], [k]S,Z,0.75[/k] to make a box that is 2m x 3m x 1.5m and [k]Ctrl-A,S[/k] to apply the scale (Image 1).

image.caption: Image 1 - Starting with a cube, scaling it to make a box that is 2m x 3m x 1.5m and applying the scale

content: [k]Shift-D[/k] to duplicate the box. At this point, we need to make a decision. on the first box, select the side edges ([k]Shift-G,L[/k] will select all edges in the shape with the same length) (Image 2). Give the first box a wide bevel with six cuts, and the second box a narrow bevel with two cuts (Image 3). The first box with its wider, more rounded edges looks like its made of a formed polymer, while the second looks like welded or bent steel. For the futuristic look, we will go with the polymer style. Delete the second box and undo your changes on the first.

image.caption: Image 2 - Duplicating the box and selecting the side edges using Shift-G to select all edges of the same length
Image 3 - Giving the first box a wide bevel with six cuts for a polymer look and the second box a narrow bevel with two cuts for a welded steel look

content: Select all side edges and give it a deep bevel with one segment (Image 4). [k]Shift-G,L[/k] to select all side edges again and bevel those with six segments (Image 5). Select the bottom edge loop and bevel with six segments (Image 6).

image.caption: Image 4 - Selecting all side edges and giving it a deep bevel with one segment
Image 5 - Selecting all side edges again and beveling them with six segments
Image 6 - Selecting the bottom edge loop and beveling with six segments

content: Select the top face and [k]Shift-D,RMB,P,S[/k] to separate it as a new object (Image 7). In Edit Mode, [k]E,0.15[/k] to make it thicker (Image 8). In Object Mode, [k]S,Shift-Z[/k] to scale it out, but then make minor adjustments to make the thickness even in the x- and y-axes (Image 9).

image.caption: Image 7 - Selecting the top face and duplicating it in place and separating it as a new object
Image 8 - Going into Edit Mode and extruding to make it thicker
Image 9 - Going to Object Mode and scaling it out while making minor adjustments to keep the thickness even in the x- and y-axes

content: Go back to the main box, select the front face and [k]Shift-D,RMB,P,S[/k] to separate it as a new object (Image 10). [k]I[/k] to inset another face in the front face (Image 11). Select the outer vertices and [k]X,V[/k] to delete them and in Object Mode [k]G,X,Shift-drag[/k] to move the face out slightly in the x-axis to get rid of the z-fighting (Image 12).

image.caption: Image 10 - Going back to the main box, selecting the front face and duplicating it in place and separating it as a new object
Image 11 - Insetting another face in the front face
Image 12 - Selecting the outer vertices and deleting them and then moving the face out slightly in the x-axis in Object Mode to get rid of the z-fighting

content: With the face selected, [k]E,0.1,-[/k] to extrude the face inside the box (Image 13). In Object Mode, select the box and add a Boolean Modifier set to Difference with the front face as the Object (Image 14). If you hide the front face now, you will see that box now has an indentation on the front side where the front face was (Image 15). As long as we don't apply the modifier, wa can move the front face around and change the section being removed (Image 16). Get the front face object back to the center and flip any normals in that need it to fix the box (Image 17).

image.caption: Image 13 - Selecting the face and extruding it inside the box
Image 14 - Going to Object Mode, selecting the box and adding a Boolean Modifier set to Difference with the front face as the Object
Image 15 - Hiding the front face to reveal the indentation on the front side of the box where the front face was
Image 16 - Moving the front face around to show how the section being removed can be changed without applying the modifier
Image 17 - Getting the front face object back to the center and flipping any normals that need it to fix the box

content: Add a Loop Cut to the front face (Image 18). Delete the left-half and add a Mirror Modifier in the x-axis (Image 19). Hide the larger box (Image 20). Use the Knife Tool to cut an edge from the top corner to the bottom edge (Image 21). Bevel the edge (Image 22).

image.caption: Image 18 - Adding a Loop Cut to the front face
Image 19 - Deleting the left half and adding a Mirror Modifier in the x-axis
Image 20 - Hiding the larger box
Image 21 - Using the Knife Tool to cut an edge from the top corner to the bottom edge
Image 22 - Beveling the edge

content: You will need to fix the corner up top (Image 23). Extrude the vertices of the corner face in the x-, y-, and z-axes and delete the extra vertices (Image 24). Edge Slide the vertex in the corner out to close the face (Image 25). Extrude those face out in the y-axis (Image 26). Hide the front face, unhide the box and review the effect (Image 27).

image.caption: Image 23 - Fixing the corner up top
Image 24 - Extruding the vertices of the corner face in the x-, y-, and z-axes and deleting the extra vertices
Image 25 - Edge Sliding the vertex in the corner out to close the face
Image 26 - Extruding those faces out in the y-axis
Image 27 - Hiding the front face, unhiding the box and reviewing the effect

content: Hide the box again and go to work on the front face, deleting and creating faces so that in the end this is the shape we have (Image 28). Move around to the back of the front faces, set the Transform Pivot Point to Individual Origins and scale in the back faces (Image 29). Go into Vertex Select Mode and try to even out the depth on all sides (Image 30). Review the effect on the box (Image 31).

image.caption: Image 28 - Hiding the box and working on the front face, deleting and creating faces to achieve the desired shape
Image 29 - Moving to the back of the front faces, setting the Transform Pivot Point to Individual Origins and scaling in the back faces
Image 30 - Going into Vertex Select Mode and evening out the depth on all sides
Image 31 - Reviewing the effect on the box

content: We need to soften the sharp edges inside the depressions, so go around to the back, select the outer edges and [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to bevel them (Image 32). Review the effect on the box again (you can really see it in Material Preview Viewport Shading) (Image 33).

image.caption: Image 32 - Going around to the back, selecting the outer edges and beveling them to soften the sharp edges inside the depressions
Image 33 - Reviewing the effect on the box in Material Preview Viewport Shading

content: Select the top face of the top and [k]Shift-D,RMB,P,S[/k] to separate it as a new object (Image 34). Go to the new top object and [k]I[/k] to inset a face (Image 35). You will have some edges that create n-gons, go to the vertices at the corners, select a group, and [k]M,A[/k] to collapse them at the center (Image 36). Repeat this all around the inset face, and merge the final corner groups to make a rectangle, and delete the outer vertices (Image 37). Move the face up slightly in the z-axis to get rid of the z-fighting (Image 38).

image.caption: Image 34 - Selecting the top face of the top and duplicating it in place and separating it as a new object
Image 35 - Going to the new top object and insetting a face
Image 36 - Going to the vertices at the corners to fix n-gons, selecting a group and collapsing them at the center
Image 37 - Repeating this all around the inset face, merging the final corner groups to make a rectangle, and deleting the outer vertices
Image 38 - Moving the face up slightly in the z-axis to get rid of the z-fighting

content: [k]E,0.1,-1[/k] to move it down into the top (Image 39). In Object Mode, select the top and add a Boolean Modifier set to Difference with the top face as the Object (Image 40). Add two loop cuts to the top face to cut it into quarters, delete the opposite vertices, and add a Mirror Modifier in the x- and y-axes (Image 41). Move the left and top edges in to create a cross shape on top (Image 42).

image.caption: Image 39 - Extruding and moving it down into the top
Image 40 - Going to Object Mode, selecting the top and adding a Boolean Modifier set to Difference with the top face as the Object
Image 41 - Adding two loop cuts to the top face to cut it into quarters, deleting the opposite vertices, and adding a Mirror Modifier in the x- and y-axes
Image 42 - Moving the left and top edges in to create a cross shape on top

content: Fill in any missing faces (Image 43). Bevel the inner corner (Image 44). Move the middle edge inwards (Image 45). Scale in the back face and bevel the edges, like you did for the front face (Image 46).

image.caption: Image 43 - Filling in any missing faces
Image 44 - Beveling the inner corner
Image 45 - Moving the middle edge inwards
Image 46 - Scaling in the back face and beveling the edges as done for the front face

content: Duplicate and separate the side face as a new object, add a vertical Loop Cut, remove the left half, add a Mirror Modifier in the x-axis, inset a small face and move it towards the top (Image 47). Delete the outside vertices, move the face out in the x-axis to fix the z-fighting, extrude inwards, and add the Boolean Modifier to the box (Image 48). Inset a small face and extrude it in (Image 49). Cut an edge on the bottom face of the extrusion and [k]S,X,0[/k] to even it out (Image 50). Extrude the bottom face up, and now you have some handles (Image 51). Feel free to bevel the inside edges if you want.

image.caption: Image 47 - Duplicating and separating the side face as a new object, adding a vertical Loop Cut, removing the left half, adding a Mirror Modifier in the x-axis, insetting a small face and moving it towards the top
Image 48 - Deleting the outside vertices, moving the face out in the x-axis to fix the z-fighting, extruding inwards, and adding the Boolean Modifier to the box
Image 49 - Insetting a small face and extruding it in
Image 50 - Cutting an edge on the bottom face of the extrusion and evening it out in the x-axis
Image 51 - Extruding the bottom face up to create handles
